text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's independent newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The designer of the logo used for the Botswana team participating in the Central African Under-17 soccer tournament has been granted an interdict preventing further use of the logo or the sale of items carrying it, until he and the Botswana Football Association come to an agreement on the sharing of profits from the sales.

- The Water Utilities Corporatiion has refuted press reports that it is to allow a Malaysian investor in partnership with a local company to build tourist accommodation throughout the country. Not only had no such tender been awarded, there was no such tender proposed.

- The diretor of Botswana's National Productivity Centre has called upon the government to speedily address a demand by manual workers for a 154-percent wage increase. The Minister for Works, Transport and Communications said that although there were no minimum wages for domestic workers and herdsmen, "they were free to negotiate with their employers for higher pay".

- The Mass Media Communications Bill will be presented at the next sitting of parliament, the permanent secretary in the Office of the President said. It would include proposed legislation for a Broadcasting Authority ad an independent Press Council.
